blocks.text: If we hold a soft rubber ball in our hand and squeeze it, the shape or volume of the ball changes; if we stop squeezing and open our hand, the ball returns to its original spherical shape (Fig. 5.1). Similarly, if we hold the two ends of a rubber string and move our hands apart, the length of the string increases under the force exerted by our hands, and the greater the applied force the larger the increase in length; on removing the force the string returns to its original length. From these examples it is concluded that deformation, a change in shape, length or volume, is produced when a body is subjected to some external force.

blocks.title: Elasticity
blocks.text: In crystalline solids atoms are usually arranged in a certain order and held about their equilibrium positions by the inter-atomic cohesive force. Under an external force distortion occurs because the atoms are displaced from their equilibrium positions, and the body is said to be in a state of stress. After the removal of the external force the atoms return to their equilibrium positions and the body regains its original shape, provided the applied force was not too great. The ability of a body to return to its original shape is called elasticity. Fig. 5.2 illustrates the deformation of a unit cell of a crystal under an external force: unstretched, under an outward stretching force, under an inward applied force, and after the force is removed.

blocks.prompt: A steel rod and a rubber band are subjected to the same force; which stretches more, and which is more elastic (Brain Teaser; MCQ 5.2)?
blocks.explanation: The rubber band stretches far more, because its Young's modulus is tiny compared with steel's. Elasticity in physics is the ability to regain the original shape, measured by how much stress is needed for a given strain, so steel, with the larger modulus, is the more elastic material.

items: Deformation (change of shape, length or volume) is produced by an external force; atoms are displaced from equilibrium (a state of stress) and return when the force is removed, if it was not too great: elasticity.
